title: From API Request to Business Result
readerIntent: Follow a typical secured operation through Nodics layers.
owner: Owning business module plus shared request, pipeline, data, and security capabilities
summary: A route enters the governed request pipeline, resolves identity and context, delegates through controller and service layers, uses authoritative models, and returns normalized status and trace context.

sections.heading: Example flow
items: The router matches method and path and declares whether authentication is required.
The request pipeline resolves tenant, authentication, authorization, headers, and request context.
The controller validates transport-level input and delegates the use case.
A facade may coordinate several services; the owning service applies business rules.
Schema item or search models apply data contracts and use configured framework providers.
Interceptors run only at declared extension points; events publish facts after the owned state transition.
The response handler maps stable status codes and trace context to the transport response.

sections.heading: Concrete example: update an enterprise
paragraphs: An authenticated employee edits an Enterprise in Axis. The browser sends the bearer or approved session-derived credential, enterprise identifier, changed fields, and current workspace context to the Profile-owned API.

The request pipeline validates exposure and headers, resolves the tenant from trusted authentication context, authenticates the employee, evaluates permissions, and attaches correlation information. A browser-supplied tenant label cannot broaden this scope.

sections.heading: Business and data execution
items: The controller maps transport data and delegates the update use case.
The Profile service loads the Enterprise through its authoritative model.
Schema and relationship rules validate fields, parent Enterprise, Tenant, addresses, and contacts.
Business logic protects ownership and any lifecycle constraints.
Persistence resolves the configured tenant-aware connection and executes through its provider.
Declared interceptors, cache invalidation, search indexing, audit, and events run at owned lifecycle points.

sections.heading: Response and observability
paragraphs: A registered success status becomes the normalized API response. Axis displays a user-friendly message and updated record. Logs and metrics correlate the request, capability, operation, duration, outcome, and safe tenant context.
Sensitive field values, credentials, tokens, and provider internals are excluded from user responses and normal diagnostics.

sections.heading: Failure behavior
items: Authentication, authorization, validation, conflict, provider, and internal failures retain distinct stable codes.
Pipeline error paths perform bounded cleanup and normalized response handling.
Logs and metrics include safe context and correlation without exposing credentials or sensitive records.

sections.heading: Failure walkthrough
items: Missing authentication stops before business execution with an authentication status.
A valid employee without update permission receives an authorization failure.
Wrong-tenant or inaccessible relationships are rejected without disclosing protected records.
Malformed fields or invalid state produce stable validation or conflict statuses.
A transient provider failure is distinguished from deterministic business rejection.
Error pipeline cleanup and response normalization execute once and preserve the original trace.

sections.heading: Deployment independence
paragraphs: The same logical flow can execute with modules in one local monoServer or across separately deployed module servers. Transport and resilience become topology concerns; capability ownership does not move.

sections.heading: Distributed execution
paragraphs: When Profile runs remotely, the calling module or frontend uses its configured API contract. Timeouts, retries, circuit behavior, and readiness protect the transport boundary. Retrying a non-idempotent mutation requires an idempotency contract.

Module self-registration with BackOffice improves discovery but is asynchronous and retryable. A temporary BackOffice outage must not move Profile ownership or block unrelated local requests after Profile is ready.

sections.heading: Verification matrix
items: Successful local and configured remote execution.
Unauthenticated, unauthorized, wrong-tenant, invalid-field, invalid-relation, and conflict behavior.
Provider timeout, dependency loss, restart, retry, and duplicate-request boundaries.
Stable statuses and safe trace context across every failure layer.
Cache, search, event, audit, and generated-contract integration.
Regression with the capability hosted in monoServer and a dedicated server.
